newsitem.title: CANADA: BHP Arctic diamond mine okay delayed.
newsitem.headline: BHP Arctic diamond mine okay delayed.

text.p: A 60-day deadline for final government approval of a diamond mine in Canada's Arctic proposed by Broken Hill Proprietary Co Ltd and Dia Met Minerals Ltd will not be met but all interested parties are hard at work negotiating a final deal, a government spokeswoman said on Monday.

"Well, it wasn't locked in stone. It wasn't a deadline. It continues to be work in progress, there is work that is going on up there," said Cate McCready, spokeswoman for Canadian Northern Development Minister Ron Irwin. "There is no announcement due today in terms of where it's at."
The Canadian government approved the project in principle in August and set a 60-day period for granting final approval. This period was due to expire around October 7.

Final government approval depends on reaching an environmental agreement between the two companies and Ottawa, which will ensure that all recommendations of an environmental review and environmental commitments are kept. BHP also has to negotiate impact benefit agreements with Native communities in the Northwest Territories.
The mine, which will be the first diamond project in Canada, is expected to cost C$860 million (US$628 million).
-- Malina Poshtova Zang, Reuters Ottawa Bureau (613) 235-6745
